definitions.explanation: A tree that is notably large in size.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}に{大木|たいぼく}がある。
examples.english: There is a large tree at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {樹齢|じゅれい}{百年|ひゃくねん}の{大木|たいぼく}が{立|た}っている。
examples.english: A hundred-year-old large tree stands there.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}で{大木|たいぼく}が{倒|たお}れた。
examples.english: A large tree fell in the typhoon.

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}の{大木|たいぼく}の{下|した}で{子供|こども}たちが{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: Children are playing under the large tree in the park.

examples.japanese: この{大木|たいぼく}は{町|まち}のシンボルとして{大切|たいせつ}にされていて、{毎年|まいとし}{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{見|み}に{来|く}る。
examples.english: This large tree is treasured as a symbol of the town, and many people come to see it every year.

notes:
{大木|たいぼく} means a large tree — notably big in trunk, height, or canopy. It evokes impressive, mature trees rather than just any large one.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {大木|たいぼく}が{立|た}つ: a large tree stands
- {大木|たいぼく}を{切|き}り{倒|たお}す: to fell a large tree
- {樹齢|じゅれい}〜{年|ねん}の{大木|たいぼく}: a tree aged ~ years

RELATED WORDS:
- {巨木|きょぼく}: giant tree (even larger, often awe-inspiring)
- {老木|ろうぼく}: old tree (emphasis on age)
- {樹木|じゅもく}: tree (formal, general term)
- {御神木|ごしんぼく}: sacred tree (at shrines/temples)

REGISTER:
Neutral to slightly formal. In casual speech, {大|おお}きい{木|き} (big tree) is more natural.
